The sensitivity guides in deformation patterns, force vs displacement curves, energy absorption, and possible applications of the modified panels.

articleTitle: An Effective Undersampling Approach to Deal with Class Imbalance Problem in Software Defect Prediction
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Machine learning based software defect prediction (SDP) approaches assist in estimating where faults are likely to occur in source code. In real-life projects, fault-free modules are higher in number than faulty modules. This is referred to as class imbalance problem. Random over-sampling and random under-sampling (RUS) are the basic sampling strategies in data-level approaches for class imbalance problem. The RUS approach removes the instances randomly and due to randomness, loss of useful information may occur. On the other hand, over-sampling may lead to biased modeling. In this paper, we propose a new technique known as Structured Under-Sampling (SUS) to address both of these problems. The proposed approach systematically removes inconsistent and redundant instances. After that, most similar instances to the existing instances are removed to ensure minimum loss of information. For empirical evaluation, C4.5 classifier has been used to compare SUS with RUS and Tomek RUS while performance difference has been analyzed using F1-score and ROC. The results of our investigation show improved performance of SUS over other approaches. Moreover, it has been observed that the Imbalance ratio (IR) affects the performance of SUS. More specifically, when IR > 5 SUS outperformed in all results.

articleTitle: A 4-Bit higher Order Tri-Band FSS With Multifunction Property at Two Bands
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This research introduces a tri-band frequency selective surface with multifunction performance at two bands. Nine different functional states are achieved with biasing to the four pin diodes. Two closely spaced bands around 2 GHz and 4 GHz furnish shift in electromagnetic behavior and inversion to plane wave polarization. The binary state "0000" contributes transmission to the dual polarized plane wave for both polarizations at pass band of 2 GHz as central frequency and shielding to the wave at pass band around 4 GHz. Conversely, the binary state "1111" contributes inverse electromagnetic behavior at these bands. The binary state "1010" contributes transmission to the TE wave at 2 GHz frequency and furnishes shielding to the 4 GHz band, whereas the binary state "0101 contributes transmission to the TM wave at 4 GHz frequency with shielding at 2 GHz. The binary state "1101 = 1110" allows to transmit the band around 4 GHz for TE wave, whereas the binary state "1011 = 0111" contributes shielding to the two multi-functional bands around 2 GHz and 4 GHz frequencies. The binary state "1011 = 0111" is inversion of the "1101 = 1110" state. The binary state "1000 = 0100" allows to transmit the band around 2 GHz for TE wave, whereas the binary state "0001 = 0010" contributes shielding to the two multi-functional bands around 2 GHz and 4 GHz frequencies. Converse is true for the binary state "0001 = 0010". The binary state "0011" = "1100" shields both the bands at 2 GHz and 4 GHz frequencies for dual polarized plane wave. All the binary states which contributes a pass band at 2 GHz also add an extra pass band around 5.9 GHz which is angularly stable at TE wave excitation only.

articleTitle: Enciphering Scheme using Planar Near-Rings and DNA Transform
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Cryptography is a ubiquitous tool used to preserve the confidentiality and integrity of the information. For this purpose, various encryption algorithms have been designed by cryptographers. Customary, in algebraic cryptography, Galois fields are focused while constructing such ciphers because of the availability of the inverse elements. However, this article presents a novel secrecy-providing algorithm using the Planar Near-Rings. Since these rings do not bear distributive law, they are suitable for achieving confusion and diffusion in enciphered data. After applying the structure of Planar Near-Rings, we apply the DNA transform in parallel, enhancing diffusion in the adjacent data bytes. In the end, the enciphered data is examined through various tests and comes out with results that guarantee the strength of the proposed scheme against numerous attacks.

articleTitle: Simulation of Ultra Short Baseline System for Positioning of Underwater Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper presents simulation of an Ultra Short Baseline (USBL) acoustic positioning system to provide range and bearing estimates of an underwater vehicle. The proposed method estimates the position of an Underwater Vehicle relative to the USBL, using the time of arrival (TOA) of underwater acoustic signals. An acoustic signal emitted from an underwater vehicle, received on an array of hydrophones, and detected using a matched filter or replica cross-correlator. This helps to determine the TOA and to estimate the position of the emitter. The system performance depends on the accurate detection of the signals received on hydrophone array and accurate TOA estimation. In shallow water environment, these received signals become distorted due to additive noise and multipath phenomena. Keeping this in view, pure tone pulse is compared with hyperbolic frequency modulated (HFM) signals resulting in improved TOA measurements with stronger multi-path and noise rejection. The performance of the proposed method is validated based on simulated USBL data with SNR level of 0 dB and bearing accuracy up to 3.22<sup>0</sup>.

articleTitle: An Improved Hybrid DC Circuit Breaker with Battery Banks for Energy Storage in HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: High voltage direct current (HVDC) power system is gaining popularity over high voltage alternating current (HVAC) systems in the area of power distribution and transmission based on their performance, reliability, efficiency, and integration with renewable. Despite its many advantages, one of the most difficult aspects of using DC is breaking its DC current, because, unlike AC, DC does not have zero-crossing. The situation becomes more worst when the source is inductive in nature. As network inductance resists a quick shift in the current. Conventional hybrid dc circuit breaker (HDCCB) topologies handle this problem by dissipating the network inductance's energy or regenerating this energy and sent back to the DC source. Moreover, previous work was limited to DC sources. However, in this paper, battery banks are introduced to store this regenerative energy of the network inductance of HDCCB irrespective of the nature of the source. Be it AC or DC. A more flexible and realistic scenario is presented and tested in the HVDC grid. In which AC source is generating power sending to HVDC transmission lines through rectifier and store that regenerated energy in battery banks during DC fault. The proposed topology has an edge over existing circuit breaker topologies, owing to battery banks that can store this regenerative energy into storage elements for future use. In addition, this topology is tested in a 500kV HVDC transmission system which will improve the overall performance of the HVDC grid. The entire system is simulated using the MATLAB/SIMULINK platform.

articleTitle: Dual Band Metasurface-based Perfect Absorber for Ku band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this paper, a reflective metasurface that can work as a metasurface based perfect absorber in microwave frequency regime is presented. The unit cell consist of star shape copper layer with a square slot printed on FR4, the thickness of substrate is 2.4mm with loss tangent 0.02 backed by a metal ground. The proposed metasurface absorbs electromagnetic (EM) waves in two frequency bands specifically at frequencies from 13.82 – 14.02 GHz and 17.65 – 17.82 GHz. The absorption efficiencies of the proposed metasurface are above 90% within the operating frequency bands. The mirror symmetry of a structure make the response of metasurface same for both transverse electric (TE) or x-polarized and transverse magnetic (TM) or y-polarized incident waves.

articleTitle: Fast Sparse Magnetic Resonance Image Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In statistical modeling, sparsity can be exploited to yield a numerically stable solution for ill-conditioned inverse problems and to increase interpretability of predictive models. Moreover, the data acquisition process and reconstruction accuracy in magnetic resonance imaging can be improved significantly using sparse modeling. In this paper, we solve, for the first time, the nonconvex ℓ<inf>0</inf>-penalized regression problem with a total variation constraint. We develop a novel and efficient algorithm to accelerate magnetic resonance imaging that yields a more accurate reconstructed image than that obtained by solving the convex relaxation problem using the ℓ<inf>1</inf> norm. We propose, for the first time, the Bayesian information criterion for model selection in neuroimaging problems. Using standard reconstruction quality metrics, we demonstrate the superiority of the proposed algorithm compared to the state-of-the-art in magnetic resonance reconstruction.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Electrical Propulsion System of Unmanned Underwater Vehicle Using MATLAB GUI
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this paper, the problem is to design and simulate an Electric Propulsion System (EPS) for Unmanned Underwater Vehicle (UUV) by doing real-time simulations using MATLAB GUI that incorporates the analysis of change in speed with respect to physical parameters of the vehicle such as drag force, power, and thrust force to be capable of doing desired missions as same as Remus-600 (UUV). For proposed EPS in which the batteries are the main power source, the electric motor will then be the driving foundation and propellers will be the driven equipment. The EPS is designed based on a study of various existing UUV around the world. MATLAB GUI based simulations has been carried out using different physical design parameters such as, current drawn from the battery, endurance, drag, thrust, RPM, etc. Finally, proposed EPS ensures the vital abilities to be more energy efficient along with high speed and enough endurance.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic NDT based method for in-situ estimation of load bearing capacity & post-cure quality assessment of carbon-epoxy composites
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The properties of composite materials are highly dependent on the layup and curing processes. Inadequate layup process and curing can lead to several type of subsurface defects. The criticality of applications and the sensitive nature of the curing process, necessitates high degree of post-curing quality assurance. Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) based methods are most suitable for such quality assessment, as no material degradation or reduction in material’s remaining useful life take place. In this study, an Ultrasonic based NDT method is developed for estimation of load bearing capacity and post-cure quality assessment of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) laminates. Traditionally, such mechanical properties are determined using Destructive Testing (DT). The presence of curing defects alters the elasticity modulus of the material and cause shift in the Ultrasonic Attenuation Coefficient (UAC). CFRP laminates with different thicknesses are developed, UAC and load bearing capability of samples are measured using UT and Bending Testing (BT) technique, respectively. Based on the tests results an empirical relationship is established between UAC and load bearing capacity of the laminates. This relationship provide means for quality assessment of the composite curing process through estimation of load bearing capacity of the laminate.

articleTitle: Numerical Study of the Interaction Mechanism of the Juxtaposed Bionic Fishes Using Immersed Boundary Method
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The migration movement of fish in regular formation is a common phenomenon in nature. Exploring the principle of hydrodynamics is not only conducive to further understanding the internal mechanism of the fish swarm, but also conducive to optimizing the structural design and formation design of underwater vehicles. The immersed boundary method used in this paper is a non-fitting Cartesian mesh method, which can better deal with the problems of complex geometric shapes and moving boundaries without generating fitting meshes as frequently as the traditional mesh generation method. In this study, a solving program is developed based on the immersion boundary direct force algorithm, which uses multi-grids and non- uniform grids to accelerate the solution of the flow field. The program is verified by a typical example of cylindrical flow, and the corresponding accuracy of the program is demonstrated through comparing the achieved results with that reported in the existing literature. Based on this verified program, the movements of the juxtaposed bionic fishes in incompressible viscous flow are analyzed, the interactions between the movements of fishes and the surrounding flow field are captured, and, importantly, the hydrodynamic mechanism of juxtaposed bionic fishes swimming in a shoal of fish is revealed. Different characteristics of flow fields induced by the juxtaposed bionic fishes’ movements with the same swing frequency but in different phases, namely in-phase and anti- phase, are observed and analyzed. The result shows that the anti- phase scenario is more beneficial to enhancing the overall propulsion performance of the shoal of fish.

articleTitle: Speed and Thermal Analysis of High-Speed Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motors are used in various applications such as robotics applications, electric vehicles (EV), electrically powered toys, etc. In consideration, such motors are exposed to tremendous thermal strain. Keeping in view the strains it is possible to control motors’ parameters by driving circuitry of such motors, minimizing the losses. To prevent heat losses of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) in electric vehicles, this paper enables the design and put into effect an analyzing scheme for a permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) which shows the behavior of the concerned motor in terms of its speed and heat losses. The sensitivity of vulnerable parameters for temperature is researched and the motor drive control system is designed to let the motor operate at bearable speed and thereby minimize the losses.

articleTitle: Harnessing the Power of Machine Learning for Mapping of Iron Oxide Mineralization using Sentinel Satellite Spectral Imagery
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In recent decades, satellite-based mineral exploration has been recognized as one of the most cost-effective and time-efficient tools for regional exploration. In this study, three advanced digital image processing techniques based on machine learning were used on multispectral Sentinel satellite data for mapping of iron oxides: Spectral Band Combination (SBC), Spectral Band Ratio (SBR), and Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM). The satellite data was preprocessed in parallel using image enhancement algorithms on high computational machines. The results demonstrated that the SAM technique was more promising and efficient for accurate mapping of iron oxide mineralization in South Africa’s Northern Cape region, with an overall accuracy of 81.62 percent. The cost-effective, robust, and efficient methodology developed in this study can explore iron oxide mineralization resources in other regions with similar geographical and geological characteristics. The findings of this study can be a starting point for developing a mine plan, along with other ground data sets from the mining regions.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Effect of Relative Humidity on Pressure Drop Across Crossflow Heat Exchanger with Staggered Tube Arrays at Its Extreme Operational Temperature
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Cross flow heat exchangers form a common and an essential component of many industrial applications and solutions. Heat exchange in these heat exchangers depends upon the Reynolds number and thermophysical properties of air and effective surface area. For the flowing cooling air, the pressure drop across the heat exchanger dictates the amount of resistance the fluid faces while flowing through it or the power needed to move the flow across the tubes. In this research, the pressure drop athwart an elliptical tubed cross flow heat exchanger available in the facility has been studied numerically at its maximum operating temperature of 323K with Reynolds number ranging from 5000 to 20000. The simulations are performed with increasing relative humidity from 0% to 80% in the cooling air. The thermophysical properties of humid air are incorporated. The relative humidity is simulated in the form of mass fractions of water vapours in the air. The effect of this change in humidity content is examined on the pressure difference between the inlet and outlet of the heat exchanger. The results depict the decline in pressure drop up to 5.5% with the increasing humidity content from 0% to 80%. The decreasing phenomenon is studied on the selected Reynolds numbers of the mentioned range. The research shows that the change in pressure drop due to increasing relative humidity in the cooling air does not depend on the Reynolds number but it depends on the moisture content present in the air. This paper provides an instrument to examine the pressure drop characteristics across cross flow heat exchangers with elliptical arrays of tubes in humid air conditions.

articleTitle: Integral Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion based Control of Input-Derivative Affine Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In recent times, development of economical yet powerful microprocessors, and increasing demands on performance characteristics have spurred great advancements in the field of nonlinear control. However, most of the nonlinear control theory and its techniques are developed for input affine systems, whereas the dynamics of many physical systems depends not only on the inputs but also on their derivatives. While this phenomenon can be easily catered for in linear systems through either state-space or transfer function representations, it is not as straightforward for nonlinear systems. In this paper, it is shown that Input-Derivative Affine (IDA) systems can be transformed to remove explicit dependency on input-derivative, but the resulting system is generally non-affine with respect to input. It is a difficult proposition to accrue nonlinear control for a non-affine system. In this paper, a novel Integral Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion (i-NDI) based control scheme is presented to deal directly with IDA systems. An example of Twin Rotor MIMO system, having strong coupling between pitch and yaw dynamics, is illustrated to demonstrate the efficacy of the presented scheme.

articleTitle: Control Satellite Orientation with Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The orientation of a satellite in space, or the correction of its trajectory is a very important problem, very topical, which requires precise movements in conditions of existence of the disturbing forces such as the forces of attraction of the earth and the moon, solar currents, variations of magnetic fields. Determining the angular motion of the existing flywheels on each of the satellite's axes, movements necessary for reorientation in space, requires knowledge of direct and inverse kinematics, as well as the inverse dynamics of the satellite. Determining the Jacobian matrix is an important step to generate the pseudo-inverse Jacobian matrix necessary to iteratively calculate the angular displacement on each axis, and the used neural network must ensure a very fine filtering of the determined values, in order to obtain the Fourier vibration spectrum and extreme accuracy.The results obtained from this research as well as the designed LabVIEW virtual instrumentation will be able to be used in the future, for similar research.

articleTitle: CFD study of Liquid slosh in Aerial Vehicle to investigate damping effects
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Sloshing of Liquid propellant in aerial vehicle can causes serious problems in stability of system which effects the flight control system operation. Sloshing act like a mechanical spring mass damper and it has to be considered while designing oil tankers, dams and fuel tanks of aerial vehicle. The objective of this work is to study the influence of baffle position in partially filled spherical body on slosh suppression. Simulation of slosh behavior is done using ANSYS-FLUENT software. A three-dimensional spherical body model was established to study the effect of damping and slosh frequency by using different positions of baffle with respect to different liquid height. A sudden initial velocity is given to tank and then tracking of free surface motion of liquid is done by using Volume of Fluid (VOF) model. Results shows that the proper position of baffle with respect to water filled level enhances the slosh damping. Moreover, water filled level also effects the slosh phenomena.

articleTitle: Design of X-rudder AUV’s Motion Control using Sliding Mode Control with Optimal Rudder Allocation Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this paper, motion control and guidance of X-rudder Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) is studied. The AUV is propelled with the help of a single thruster. In order to achieve motion in all directions, X-rudder is included, which offers better maneuverability and safety as compared to other types of rudders. This design approach offers efficient maneuverability and motion control, however with various challenges with respect to its implementation. Decoupled mathematical model of the AUV in 3 DOF horizontal subsystem is utilized and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) technique is used to design motion control. In order to achieve desired heading of the vehicle, an optimal control allocation problem is solved based on a virtual control input by allocating distributed control effort on each of the 4 fins of the X-rudder to create cumulative desired control input. Furthermore, a constrained optimization method is applied for optimal angle calculation for rudder fins keeping in view either of two objectives i.e. minimum control effort (energy efficient) or minimum desired heading error. Detailed simulation results are presented for performance analysis of the proposed control framework.

articleTitle: Cost effective catalytic degradation of Methylene blue (MB) using Zero valent iron nanoparticles (ZVFeNPs)
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The aim of this work was to effectively degrade hazardous dye methylene blue (MB) using zero valent iron metal nanoparticles (ZVFeNPs) and comparative analysis were made with bulk iron metal ions. Nanotechnology has brought an ease by providing ways to synthesize various nanomaterials. One of the suitable catalyst is zero valent iron metal nanoparticles which are synthesized by chemical reduction method. Advantage of using zero valent iron nanoparticles (ZVFeNPs) is that they are easy to synthesize and are stored as solid. These nanoparticles are cost effective and eco-friendly. Oxidation of Methylene blue (MB) was used as model reaction. MB was degraded in the presence of potassium peroxydisulfate (K<inf>2</inf>S<inf>2</inf>O<inf>8</inf>) as an appropriate oxidizing agent using zero valent iron nanoparticles as catalyst in acidic medium. The reaction was followed using spectrophotometer at 663nm. Reaction kinetics was observed during initial 30 minutes. Statistical error functions were also evaluated to determine the precision of the results and various thermodynamic parameters were also obtained. Zero valent iron nanoparticles (ZVFeNPs) are versatile in their function and used for such type of the degradation with many other dyes. Zero Valent iron nanoparticles are highly stable, work better under acidic medium and performed better than their bulk iron metal ions. In future, these nanoparticles can be beneficial for the elimination of toxic dyes from industrial effluent treatment.

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Control of a Quadrotor: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper presents a performance comparison of PID, linear and nonlinear active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) for a quadrotor based on robustness, disturbance rejection and control actuation. ADRC being model independent is suitable for systems like quadrotor, for which system parameters are not precisely known and dynamics are prone to external disturbances. Its notable features such as error-driven control law, extended state observer and a nonlinear feedback law, makes ADRC a suitable candidate for dealing with disturbances and uncertainties, while minimizing control actuation concurrently. Nonlinear simulations have been carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of controllers. To check robustness, a Monte-Carlo analysis with different sets of parametric uncertainties has been performed. Furthermore, a disturbance analysis has been carried out to demonstrate disturbance rejection capability. The simulation results are discussed based on the performance of designed controllers and their corresponding control actuation. The results reveal that nonlinear ADRC has an edge over both linear ADRC and PID as it deals effectively with disturbances and uncertainties while minimizing the control energy.

articleTitle: Prevalence, bacteriology and antimicrobial susceptibility of bacteria associated with cattle and buffaloes mastitis in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa during 2020-21
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Mastitis, "inflammation of the mammary gland", is economically devastating disease of dairy industry and also a significant disease of public health importance. The bearing of various bacteria in milk renders it objectionable for human consumption, which also might be a source of spreading of tuberculosis, staphylococcal infection and toxins, streptococcal sore throat, gastroenteritis and brucellosis. Additionally, diseases like bovine mastitis and reproductive infections in dairy animals are also important reasons for the usage of antimicrobial agents for frequent and prolonged durations, thus it contributes considerably to the dissemination of multi-drug resistant (MDR) bacteria. Therefore, this study was carried out to investigate the prevalence of bacterial pathogens associated with cattle and buffaloes mastitis and their antimicrobial susceptibilities. Milk samples (n = 1166) from cattle (n = 870) and buffaloes (n = 296) were processed during 2020-21. Besides, 821 mastitic samples were further processed for bacteriology and antimicrobial susceptibility test by disc diffusion method. The results showed a prevalence of 17.9% clinical mastitis in cattle and 10.8% in buffaloes. Subclinical mastitis was 69% in cattle and 79.4% in buffaloes. The most prevalent bacteria associated with mastitis were Escherichia coli (34%) and Staphylococci spp. (26%). Some other bacteria were Streptococci spp. (8%), Salmonella spp. (5%), Klebsiella spp. (5%), Pasturella spp. (4%) and Bacillus spp. (0.1%). The bacterial isolates were mostly resistant to streptomycin (97%), sulphamethoxazole (94%), penicillin (91%), and oxytetracycline (91%). However, high susceptibilities were noted in case of agents like gentamycin (87%), enrofloxacin (86%), and florfenicol (69%). This study may suggest high prevalence of mastitis in cattle and buffaloes caused by various bacteria, which were found highly resistant to various antimicrobial agents

articleTitle: Computational Fluid Mechanics Model for Numerical Investigation of Frictional Tribo-pair during Mixed Lubrication
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: All the machines are constructed through mechanical links and pairs. One of the crucial pairs is the sliding pair; due to their nature and general use, they are often subjected to a higher degree of dynamics and external forces leading to high frictional force. To reduce wear from friction formerly thick film of commercial oil is used. However, viscosity-based higher thickness yields higher energy losses, and nano-lubricants are popular in reducing friction while keeping film thickness and improving wear resistance. This paper develops a numerical model for sliding pairs that predicts the load carried by components under different lubrication regimes. The aim is to simulate hydrodynamic and mixed lubrication regimes for different loading conditions. A detailed multiphysics model of tribo-pair was modeled, including lubricant rheology, surface topology, oil film squeeze, and film temperature through the moving mesh. The fluid domain has been meshed with Arbitrary Lagrangian and Eulerian techniques. Energy loss due to viscous friction and boundary friction were determined by solving Naiver- Stokes equations in the moving mesh deformable geometry domain. The numerical model was compared with the available literature, and the results are presented. This numerical simulation remained valid and provides the fundamental understanding of oil film thickness and load-carrying capacity of sliding tribo-pair in the presence of nano-lubricants. The developed model is a useful methodology for studying lubricant oil enriched with nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Computationally Efficient Numerical Analysis for Hanssen’s Disease Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Communicable diseases cause major impacts on public health system of anycommunity. The spread and outbreaks of these diseases also influence the social and economic structure of any country. Modeling the transmission dynamics of communicable diseases have become a hot area of research snice last two decades. Many researchers including mathematicians, computer scientists and data scientists putting lot of efforts to study the spread pattern of infectious diseases in various populations.This paper presents a computationally efficient numerical analysis for the dynamical behavior of Leprosy which is also known as Hanssen’s Disease. Standard finite difference schemes are generally dependent on time, step size, and the choice of other model parameters as well. These schemes do not exhibit the true behavior of an infectious disease in a population. Besides, losing some essential features of the model, these schemes may also diverge in certain scenarios. To overcome these difficulties, a novel scheme in non-standard finite difference settings is proposed to analyses the spread pattern of Hanssen’s Disease. Numerical experiments are performed using MATLAB and a comparison with standard finite difference schemes is also presented. The proposed schemes is turned out to be more reliable, preserves all the essential features and remains consistent with the biological nature of continuous Hanssen’s Disease model.

articleTitle: High Performance C-band Power Amplifier for CW and Pulsed Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper demonstrates design, fabrication and measurements of GaN-HEMT based power amplifier (PA) for pulsed radar applications. The purpose of this effort is to design and develop a class- AB PA using GaN HEMT device to get the wide dynamic range upto 80dB (i.e., -50 to 30dBm) in a compact size for C-band pulsed applications. It can also be employed as a driver and power stage for C- band applications with pulse modulation requirement upto 40 dBm. In PA design, oscillations are common which caused the unwanted high gain at the lower frequencies. To avoid this scenario, capacitor bank is used at the bias. Impedance transformers both at the input and output of the amplifier are implemented to achieve optimized parameters such as high RF power, high power gain and good input/output return losses etc. The proposed amplifier is fabricated and then characterized to verify the design parameters successfully. It has been observed that the simulated results are in good agreement with the measured readings. Maximum RF pulsed power output of 10W (40dBm), power gain of 12dB and dynamic range of 80dB are demonstrated for C-band applications.

articleTitle: Molecular Dynamics Evolution for Thermal Conductivity of Complex Yukawa Liquids
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The calculation of thermal properties of complex liquids is a significant work. Thermal conductivity (λ) of complex liquids (dusty plasmas) has been computed using Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations by including polarization effect. The polarization effects on thermal conductivity along with different system sizes has been calculated for a wide series of Coulomb coupling (Γ) and Debye screening (κ) parameters using MD method. Accurate results are obtained using this algorithm with small dimension and quick convergence effects. The results have been contrasted with other accessible MD simulation results, theoretical assumptions, and with experimental findings of complex dusty plasma liquids. It is expected to demonstrate that it has better than those obtained in former known numerical methods. Moreover, it has been obtained that the present MD method has greater performance than previous numerical techniques. The newly proposed model checked in terms of accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: Particle Resolved Direct Numerical Simulations of Spouted Bed
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Spouting condition in a rectangular packed bed is investigated by particle resolved direct numerical simulations and experiments. Interactions between fluid and particles are modeled by body force type Immersed Boundary Method (IBM) and interactions between particles and particles and wall interactions are modeled using Discrete Element Method (DEM). Jet velocity is increased in steps in both simulation and experiment until a coherent and stable jet is formed. After obtaining this condition some of the characteristics of spouted bed are investigated. Because of the associated computational cost, the fluid grid is not refined beyond eight grids per particle diameter which enables only qualitative comparison between experiment and simulation. Some of the characteristics of spouted bed like minimum spouting velocity, void variations, spout shape and circulation patterns are studied in this paper.

articleTitle: Investigation of performance parameters in Rotating Wings
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The loss of efficiency due to the wingtip vortex was a well-known phenomenon in the aerospace industry. In the case of aircraft, it manifests as the induced drag, whereas in the case of rotary-wing, the vortices form a corkscrew wash and the vortices remain attached to the blade for several rotations. This affects performance parameters, and the blade vortex interaction (BVI) can occur due to the interaction of the trailing vortices of the blade with the other preceding blade. These trailing vortices can cause significant variation in the velocity field, resulting in an unsteady structural load and noise. Helicopters operating near the ground can cause entrainment of dust particles on the ground, affecting the pilot's field of view. This study aims to devise an experiment to measure performance parameters for rotating wings by varying at different pitch angles and RPM. These performance parameters include the coefficient of thrust and torque. This performance measurement was compared with past studies, and the maximum figure of merit from theory was measured to be 0.24. It was found maximum for a pitch angle of 10°, and a drop in the figure of merit was observed due to the stall of the rotating wing. A Numerical scheme was used to analyze sectional pressure on the blade surface. This numerical approach was validated, and then this approach was used to analyze the case of pitch angle 12.5° and RPM of 2000. The results computed from the numerical scheme were used to find the thrust coefficient and pressure coefficient on different sections, which compare well with the variation in mesh size. Error in coefficient of thrust was observed to be up to 5%.

articleTitle: Study on Opposing Jet Simulation of Near Space Supersonic Vehicle Based on DSMC Method
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: There are serious aerodynamic heating and high resistance phenomena for near space supersonic aircraft. Application of opposing jet flow is an effective technology for drag and heat reduction. This paper uses DSMC method to simulate the external opposite flow of aircraft moving in the supersonic flow in rarefied environment of near space. It analyzes the advantages and disadvantages of drag and heat reduction of opposing jet in the different conditoins by adjusting speeds of the jet in order to obtain an optimized scheme. The numerical results show that the peak values of aircraft surface pressure, surface heat flux and friction are reduced by 76.6%, 93.5% and 50.0% respectively. Application of opposing jet in rarefied environment can effectively reduce the drag and aerodynamic heating for supersonic aircraft. The present study provides an effective reference for the aircraft design on the drag and heat reduction.

articleTitle: GNSS Fault Detection and Exclusion Algorithm for Single Frequency Receivers
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems are widely used in numerous industries for positioning, navigation, and timing applications. Nevertheless, there are multiple factors that affect its positioning and dilute its overall accuracy. GNSS performance is characterized by four parameters which include Availability, Continuity, Accuracy, and Integrity. To ensure the best performance, integrity of the system is one of the most important factors to be monitored. In this paper we’ve proposed an integrity monitoring algorithm for single frequency GNSS receivers that detects and identify faulty measurements. Once the faulty satellite is identified, it is excluded from the measurements to ensure reliable outputs. Finally, the results of before and after the exclusion of faulty satellites are compared to ensure positioning accuracy.

articleTitle: Characterizing Beat Terrain Fluctuations in Ranging the Leaky Sensor of FMCW Transceiver
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In FMCW based leaky sensor application, a static filed being always returned as beats, develops a ranging profile, even in the absence of an intrusion. The constant presence of beats and their environment dependent gain fluctuations impose great challenge in detection of a potential threat. This paper proposes a methodology to detect the presence of an intruder by adaptively analyzing the probability distribution profile of each range bin, suppressing the ranging clutter and identifying the true intrusion zone. The algorithm adapts to a detection baseline to discriminate the human intruder from trees, grass and other environment variable as rain, wind etc. The developed scheme is realized on NI-transceiver card, VSG and leaky sensor cable. It is observed that the beat gain fluctuations are highly depended on chosen integration length, leaky sensor separation and received clutter power. The algorithm performance is evaluated through simulations and NI-equipment based field deployment. It is concluded that the proposed method effectively adapts to the leaky sensor’s environment and settles the intrusion detection profile among glitches and environment fluctuations. It is field tested over 100m range.

articleTitle: "Approximate Multipliers Based on Low-Power 4:2 Compressors for Error-Tolerant Applications"
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Energy-efficient and high-performance general- purpose compute engines, as well as application specific integrated circuits, are highly demanded to facilitate the development of artificial intelligence and big data processing applications. However, with the end of Dennard’s scaling and Moore’s law it is becoming difficult to handle massive amounts of data and complex computations required in these applications. Approximate computing (AC) has emerged as an attractive paradigm in the digital design to address this unprecedented challenge. AC is driven by the observation that many state-of-the-art applications, such as classification, machine learning, data mining, robotics and communication, exhibit error-tolerant characteristics; therefore, a small amount of error (trades off the requirement of exact computation) can be introduced to achieve area, power, and speed benefits. AC techniques can be applied at both the software and hardware layers. At the hardware layer, arithmetic units (multipliers, adders, and dividers) are considered as hardware computational modules. Therefore, the approximation at hardware layer has been focused around the design of approximate arithmetic units. This paper presents approximate multipliers based on novel 4:2 compressors for error-tolerant applications. The proposed 4:2 compressors exhibit zero-mean error behavior while having a comparable hardware utilization with the existing state-of the-art designs. The hardware-efficient as well as the error-efficient designs of variable accuracy-power has been investigated to explore the maximum trade-off. All the designs are synthesized using Cadence Genus synthesis tool (TSMC 65 nm technology) and power is reported using Cadence Joules RTL power solution. A comprehensive error analysis is performed using well-known error metrics such as error distance (ED), mean average distance (MED), mean relative error distance (MRED) and normalized mean error distance (NMED). Moreover, all the designs are also compared with respect to power-delay product (PDP) and MRED to apprehend which designs are lying on the error-energy Pareto- optimal curve. A case study is also presented to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed designs in practical image processing application.

articleTitle: Effect of Lateral Pressure on the Strength of Friction Stir Welding (FSW)
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Friction Stir welding has been done on low melting and high thermal conductivity metals. Welding is a fabrication process that connects materials, typically metals or thermoplastics, by inducing fusion, which is distinct from lower temperature metal-joining techniques such as brazing and soldering. Extensive research is underway to mature the friction stir welding process. Researchers have performed experiment to find the effect of pin tool geometry on the strength of the welded joints and effects of variables i-e forces, feed rates and rpm. This research comprises the study of lateral pressure effect on friction stir welding and to find the best optimized lateral pressure. whereas, best parameters of welding were chosen. The purpose of this research is just to highlight the effect of different factor parameters on the friction stir welding. Stir welding was performed at 1000 rpm of spindle speed, 8 mm/min of traverse speed, 72, 62, 52 MPa lateral pressures generated by applying torque and 110x50mm plate made up of AA6061-T6 with 5mm thickness. In this work the effect of lateral pressure has been used to influence tensile strength and hardness attributed to friction stir welded AA6061-T6 butt joints. The H 13 tool steel included distinct pin geometry; simple cylindrical (SC) shape was used for welding. Maximum tensile strength and hardness of 79 MPa and 66 HV was achieved at tool rotation 1000 rpm, tool feed 8 mm/min, and pressure 72 MPa. Hardness and tensile strength improved on increasing applied pressure during friction stir welding.

articleTitle: A Compact Monopulse Circularly Polarized Slot Array Antenna for Airborne Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In most advanced communication systems, radio frequency (RF) front ends having high power capability, high gain, and low-profile antenna systems are desired. In this paper, a small, lightweight, high gain with improved impedance bandwidth and circularly polarized slotted waveguide array antenna with mono-pulse capability in Ku-band is presented. Target application of presented research is on-board radio links for airborne platforms such as Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) with built-in tracking capability. The antenna presented in this study has three key components: a comparator network, a radiating slot array and a polarizer. Slotted waveguide arrays with longitudinal slots have linear polarization. Therefore, a multi-layer meta-surface based low cost polarizer is used to convert linearly polarized (LP) wave of antenna aperture into to radiating circularly polarized (CP) wave. The designed polarizer is a combination of meander and strip lines on thin dielectric substrates. The designed antenna is operating at 15 GHz and simulated using Advance Electromagnetic (EM) Simulation software. It is a an array of 6 × 8 radiating slots having peak gain >22 dB at 15 GHz, reflection bandwidth of 1200 MHz, axial ratio band-width >2 GHz and single plane mono-pulse capability. Polarizer has square shape unit cell of dimensions 5.1 mm×5.1 mm. The complete antenna including feed network and polarizer is compact with dimensions of 11 cm×11 cm×9 cm that makes it easy to house on an aircraft.

articleTitle: Model-based Performance Analysis and Health Monitoring of a Low Bypass Ratio Turbofan Engine
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this paper, a methodology is presented to develop models for a Condition Based Modelling techniques using Gas Path Analysis for a typical military engine. The baseline engine model is developed using the known aero-thermodynamic parameters of the engine in Numerical Propulsion System Simulation (NPSS). First, the sensitivity of the gas turbine engine’s performance to the efficiency of each gas path component is studied. Naturally, the engine’s performance is determined to be highly sensitive to the fluctuation in performance of the compressor, turbine, and burner modules. The response of the model to simulated faults in these critical components is then studied. The observations are made in terms of data available during engine test bed operation. The observations show a good correlation with the Fault Correlation Matrix available from the original manufacturer. The developed model and technique can be used for subsequent development of a predictive or condition-based diagnostic tool for any gas turbine engine. Furthermore, this technique can be extended to develop models for online fault diagnosis during aircraft operation, thus reducing the time and cost overhead of the conventional techniques that require extensive man-hours and downtime of the aircraft.

articleTitle: An axisymmetric supersonic nozzle computational flow analysis for a ground test facility
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: An axisymmetric convergent-divergent nozzle of Mach 5 for a high-speed ground test facility is computationally investigated in this study. CD nozzle profile design process was initiated by generating an inviscid contour of the nozzle and its performance was studied using CFD simulations by monitoring of velocity and Mach number distribution along the nozzle centre-line. Later, in order to determine flow viscous effects, viscous CFD simulations of the same profile is performed to gauge the boundary layer thickness growth along the length of the nozzle. Based on the maximum boundary layer thickness of the nozzle exit, the nozzle contour is adjusted to achieve the design Mach number at a given pressure ratio. Further, specific to its ground application usage, nozzle length optimization was performed based on a criteria of optimal flow parameters comparison at the nozzle exit plane. CFD results of the redesigned and optimized nozzle contour depicts good flow quality in the core flow region, where Mach number variation is found to be less than 0.5%, total temperature <1% and total pressure variation <0.5% with indirect benefits in reduction of its mass and material cost.

articleTitle: Heat Transfer in Gas-Solid Flows Using Direct Numerical Simulations
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this paper, an immersed boundary method (IBM) is proposed for heat transfer and fluid velocity calculation in the particulate system. In IBM, solid particles are treated as sources of velocity and temperature and Navier-Stokes equations and energy equation are solved on fixed Cartesian grid. For benchmarking of simulation results, various test cases from literature are studied. In the test cases, good agreement is observed between simulation and literature results.

articleTitle: A Compact Highly Isolated MIMO Antenna Design for WiFi-6E & 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: A 12-ports multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna design is proposed. The design is self-isolated and integrates three frequency bands namely sub-6 GHz, WiFi-6E and millimeter-wave band. The proposed design consists of six dual-band monopole slot antennas and six dual function tapered slot antennas. The monopole slot antenna works in 3.422-3.675 GHz (5G) band and 6.25-7.15 GHz (WiFi-6E) band, while the tapered slot antenna covers the 23-30 GHz band. The tapered slot works as a decoupling structure at lower frequencies as well as a slot antenna at 24GHz and 28 GHz. The design structure has an overall volume of 103.5mm×103.5mm×0.51mm. The results show satisfactory MIMO performance. The maximum value of envelop correlation coefficient is 0.124 and the minimum isolation is more than -20 dB. The realized gain is 3 dBi, 5.7 dBi, 9 dBi, and 10.3 dBi at 3.5 GHz, 6.6 GHz, 24 GHz, and 28 GHz respectively. The proposed structure is planar, simple, and compact, thus suitable for wireless devices such as future access points.

articleTitle: Radar Cross Section Based Shape Optimization of Chine Forebody
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Chine forebodies are frequently used in high-performance aircraft designs to improve stealth characteristics. However, a good design process requires construction and exploration of design space before finding optimal configuration. In this research, a chine forebody is parameterized through Bezier curves. The control points are varied through the design of experiment (DOE) approach to construct a design space. The radar-cross-section (RCS) of each configuration in design space is evaluated through the potent Computational Electromagnet-ics (CEM) tool. Subsequently, a response surface methodology (RSM) is adopted to find the optimal position of control points. The results indicate a significant reduction in RCS from the baseline case. Around 79.42% reduction in RCS was observed after optimization. The approach/pipeline defined in this paper can be extended to other surfaces with manageable computational cost and complexity.

articleTitle: Hydrocarbon Sweet Spots Detection Using Advanced Inverted Acoustic Approach in Offshore Indus Basin, Pakistan
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Pakistan lacks oil and gas resources, and its offshore areas are underexplored. As a result, no commercial oil and gas resources have yet been discovered in offshore areas. The offshore Indus basin's oil and gas resource potential was determined through inverted acoustic seismic data and stratigraphic correlation. Based on extensive inverted results, it has been determined that the area is enriched with unconventional economic hydrocarbon resources with numerous shows of sweet spots. There exist also effective tectonic-lithologic traps with the impacts of structural impacts obvious on seismic profiles. As a result, it is possible to conclude that the offshore Indus basin has viable oil and gas occurrences. There is an urgent need to improve the acquisition and processing quality of seismic data in order to fully harness the offshore Indus basin's hydrocarbon potential. In this study comprehensive review of new technologies required to be focused for indigenous development of seismic data acquisition and processing systems are presented. Strategies required to develop such technologies are crystallized to enhance the accuracy of acoustic inversion-based prediction for offshore oil and gas exploration in Pakistan Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)

articleTitle: Transmission of Cough Aerosols in a Hospital Room Related to COVID-19
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The COVID-19 coronavirus outbreak in recent years has become a pandemic across the globe. Which has a significant risk on human health causing nearly 5 million deaths worldwide. Recent research has shown that aerosol transmission is the main cause of COVID-19 virus spread. Sanitization of hands or the 6 feet at a recommended distance by WHO can reduce the virus but people with greater occupancy are needed to be addressed. A vulnerable place for disease infection is a hospital room where many patients have been infected with COVID-19. Transmission of the virus is the main cause of COVID-19 spread. Thus, understanding the flow physics of virus transmission through CFD analysis is necessary. A Euler-Lagrangian model is used to investigate aerosol transmission from an infected person inside a hospital room under the effect of ventilation. Ventilation plays a great role in the removal of aerosols from an enclosed environment. UDF was applied to turn the ventilation on after the coughing. Results have shown that without ventilation the aerosols are reaching the outlets of the room faster, while due to the ventilation effect the same aerosols reach slower due to recirculation. Aerosols travel according to the dominant ventilation flow. If the ventilation is turned off and there is no steady downward movement of air, the particles do not fall to the ground but will evaporate with time. Evaporation of the particles depends on the ambient temperature and relative humidity. The existence of running ventilation is required to prevent the circulation of aerosols.

articleTitle: Convex and Nonconvex Approaches for the Matrix Completion Problem
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Missing data is a common occurrence in modern applications such as medical imaging and movie ratings data sets for recommendation systems. Matrix completion is a procedure for recovering the missing entries in a matrix on the basis of the known entries. It is assumed that there is a linear relationship between the rows or columns of the matrix to be recovered, i.e., a small number of rows (or columns) can be used to represent the whole matrix. The matrix completion problem cannot be solved uniquely without imposing constraints such as the low-rank assumption. There are two classes of optimization techniques for sparse matrix completion, namely convex and non-convex approaches. Under the weak assumption that the matrix entries are missing in a non-uniform and deterministic fashion, the matrix completion problem can be formulated as a non-convex bilinear optimization problem that can be solved via the alternating proximal algorithm. On the other hand, the soft-impute algorithm is a convex optimization approach that can deliver fast convergence by exploiting warm-start. In this paper, we test the (convex) soft-impute and (non-convex) alternating proximal matrix completion methods using some real data and furthermore, test [1]’s claim that non-convex approaches perform better than convex approaches. We show a comparison of the two approaches in terms of computational complexity, execution time, and prediction accuracy. In addition, we propose a systematic procedure to perform model selection in both algorithms.

articleTitle: Optimized Dual Loop Control Strategy for Grid-Connected Interleaved Inverters
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The topology of interleaved inverters is preferred over conventional two-level inverters because of reduced current harmonics due to its ripple cancellation effect and high power rating through paralleling of low power devices with improved availability. This topology also reduces the filter components’ size compared to conventional 2-level inverters, resulting in increased bandwidth and high harmonic impedance to the utility distortion. However, interleaved topology requires a more complex control strategy to maintain the current regulation and system stability. When an LCL filter is used, the control strategy becomes even more complex because of its resonance phenomena. This paper presents a two-loop analysis for grid-connected interleaved inverters with LCL filters. The outer loop regulates the current and ensures reference tracking, while the inner loop improves the stability and dampens the resonance. Stability analysis and the effect of harmonic impedance offered to the grid voltage by inner feedback variables are discussed in detail. Using a dual-loop control strategy, both controller and LCL filters are optimized with the help of a genetic algorithm. The filter is minimized such that the THD of the output current is below the limit set by IEEE 1547 Std. Moreover, the controller is optimally tuned to offer maximum attenuation to the current harmonics. The system that includes an interleaved inverter along with the proposed control scheme and optimized filter has been implemented in MATLAB Simulink. Simulation results presented show the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: The Effect of Residual Stress in Welding Stainless Steel Bent Sections
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In manufacturing processes, residual stresses are generated as the base material experiences external forces. In welding, the rapid heating and cooling cycle produces shrinkage forces. These shrinkage forces produce strains and hence stresses up to the yield strength of the material are locked into the base metal. In bending of metal plates, the bent portion is permanently deformed. This deformed portion contains residual stresses. When these bent metal plates having residual stress are welded together, a complex state of residual stress is therefore observed. In the present work, simulation of both the bending and the welding processes is performed through Finite Element Analysis (FEA) to study the effect of residual stresses. A sequential simulation procedure is adopted with the results of welding analysis imposed on bending analysis. The base material selected for this study is SS 430. The overall residual stress and distortion are compared between a bent steel angle and an extruded angle welded to the base plate.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Cloud based QR Coded Watermarking DLP system
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Despite hectic security efforts in place today by large organizations, data breaches continue to occur, and identity theft is on the rise. Data leak prevention (DLP) is a suite of technologies aimed at restricting the loss of sensitive information that occurs in enterprises across the globe. By focusing on the location, classification, and monitoring of information at rest, in use and in motion, this solution can go far in helping an enterprise get a handle on what information it has, and in stopping the numerous leaks of information that occur each day. In this paper, first we suggest a policy for an enterprise to work on to prevent the data leakage and detection, depending upon access control and data location using QR code-based watermarking. QR code-based watermarking have been implemented using image and pdf files for detecting violations in accessed, downloaded, and uploaded files to central portal.

articleTitle: Optimization of Al-Cu Friction Stir Welding Parameters Through RSM and BOA
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In the automobile industry, the use of aluminum has increased with the need for lightweight and robust structures. In situations where an interface of aluminum with other materials like copper and steel is required, solid state welding process such as Friction Stir Welding (FSW) is very useful. In this research, an aluminum to copper dissimilar metal FSW welded joint is studied. The welding parameters required for joining Aluminum and Copper are optimized through Response Surface Method (RSM) and a novel optimization technique called Butterfly Optimization Algorithm (BOA). In the first phase, the critical friction stir welding parameters are tabulated. A series of welding simulations are carried out to determine temperature profile achieved through these parameters. The design of experiment approach is used to run regression analysis through response surface method. In the second phase, Butterfly Optimization Algorithm is applied to optimize the process parameters. The weld parameters optimized through BOA give an improved temperature profile to create a sound weld. Weld samples are prepared to validate the results. The tool rotational speed is found to be the major contributor in defining the temperature profile of base plates.

articleTitle: System Identification and Yaw Control of an Inspection Class ROV
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This work describes the design and real-time implementation of a yaw controller for a custom-built underwater vehicle. As opposed to the traditional mathematical-based modeling methodology, system identification approach is used for the purpose of dynamic characterization of the ROV. A proportional-integral controller is developed based on the resultant vehicle model. A unique root-locus approach is used for controller tuning. The proposed technique aids in analyzing the impact of simultaneous change in more than one parameter on the response of the system. Simulations followed by real-time experiments in pool settings demonstrate the effectiveness of the modeling and proposed control scheme employed.

articleTitle: Robust Optimal Control and Trajectory Tracking of an Unmanned Aerial Aquatic Vehicle (UAAV)
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This research paper is based on robust optimal control and trajectory tracking problem of a submarine launched Unmanned Aerial Aquatic Vehicle (UAAV). Kinematic Model of UAAV is considered with a study of its maneuvering and dynamics. Starting with a 6-DOF non-linear model of an UAAV, its motion is decoupled in longitudinal planes for various phases. An optimal control technique is proposed for underwater launch phase in which input-output feedback linearization is used to cancel system nonlinearities and then optimal control is synthesized by solving ARE. Similarly, an Optimal Sliding Mode Control is proposed for the boost phase. Stability analysis is included to validate the designed controller performance. Results of the designed tracking/guidance and control strategies are presented through the simulations.

articleTitle: FSI simulation of water entry impact of three-dimensional rigid AUV under different initial parameters
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: High speed water entry of Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) is highly transient and complex process and are subjected to huge impact loads which may cause structural damage to the AUV and inner sensitive equipment. Therefore, accurate modeling of the phenomenon, trajectory calculation and accurate prediction of hydrodynamic impact loads of vehicle at various launch conditions are of paramount importance. In this article, we study the impact characteristics of air launched AUV under different initial parameters during high speed water entry. For this purpose, numerical model based on coupled explicit finite element method (FEM) and arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian (ALE) scheme is established. ALE method is suitable for large deformation FSI simulations because it encompasses both Lagrange and Euler formulation. The fluid motion is analyzed in the Eulerian formulation, whereas the Lagrangian method is used to track the movement of vehicle and the free surface. The reliability of the applied numerical model is verified by the experimental results of the earlier study. Then, the influence of angle of attack (AOA), initial pitching moment and variation in AUV mass on water entry of rigid AUV are investigated. It is observed that impact loads rises with the increase in the attack angle. Radial load is more sensitive to change of AOA. Results also show that, for negative AOA, radial force of AUV alters its direction after initial impact. It is also witnessed that the vehicle mass has significant effect on the impact load. Some linear and nonlinear relationships between the impact characteristics and initial launch parameters are deduced. The research conclusions provide guidance for the design of AUV by selecting appropriate water entry conditions.

articleTitle: Node Embedding over Attributed Bipartite Networks in Dynamic Context
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This work seeks an effective embedding representation by the exploitation of both the structure and attribute aspect of attributed bipartite networks in a dynamic context. Most of the plain or attributed network embedding works are limited to the static type homogeneous networks, but in reality, networks often evolve that certainly effect the node homophilic relations. Hence, we propose DABNE embedding framework that investigates the dynamics of evolved nodes/links over time through targeting both the explicit and implicit node interactions of different and same entity types of a bipartite network. Primarily, it targets the dynamics of the network (structural change) and dynamics on the network (explicit/implicit node interactions either through structure or attributes similarities) on the network. We adopt the KL divergence method to model the node’s explicit interactions, and for implicit node interactions, we employ the Skipgram model. Lastly, we concatenate these independently learned latent embeddings to perform the classification (multi-class and multi-label) and clustering task. Experiments are conducted on two real-world networks with both structure and attributed based embedding methods to corroborate the efficacy of our proposed framework.

articleTitle: Research on electrical performance enhancement technology in splice area of large assembled radome
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the splicing area (reinforcement rib/joints) of large fabricated radome affects the electrical performance of enclosed antenna, this paper focuses on three methods to improve the electrical performance of these areas. Optimization of the electrical performance improvement by applying metallic wire grid electrical tunable unit, frequency selective surface (FSS) loaded in splice area and graded material. Compared with the single-layer dielectric in splicing area, these methods show different performance improvements, in which the application of FSS structure can better improve the transmission characteristics of electromagnetic waves.

articleTitle: Dynamic Nonlinear Buckling Of Viscoelastic Plate Allowing For Higher Order Modes
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The chaotic theory is employed to investigate the dynamic stability of viscoelastic plate with geometry nonlinearity. The influence of high order modes on buckling of viscoelastic plate is considered. The dynamic buckling of viscoelastic plates subject to in-plane periodic load is studied. The von-Karman nonlinear geometry equations are introduced and the linear viscoelastic model is employed. For the sake of obtaining more accurate result, the deflection is described as a trigonometric series with 4 terms instead of single term. The sign of the biggest Lyapunov exponent of the motion is employed to determine the stability of viscoelastic plate. Comparison is made between the 4 items results and 1 term results.

articleTitle: Context-Aware Neural Machine Translation using Selected Context
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Context-aware neural machine translation has attracted much attention recently by promising sophisticated contextual information integration into conventional neural machine translation. However, context-aware NMT is challenged with effective context aggregation and increased training time due integration of extra information. In this work, we study the effect of encoding selective contextual information using pre-trained models for effective contextual integration and performance optimization. We conduct experiments on different context selection methods and quantify that encoding selected context significantly reduces the training time while maintaining superiority over sentence-level NMT models. Specifically, we experimented on IWSLT English↔German translation task and show encoding selected keywords as context is sufficient and obtains best translation results.

articleTitle: An Effective Jamming Suppression Method against DRFM based Complex Range False Targets
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This work concentrates on the suppression of complicated digital radio frequency memory (DRFM) range false targets (RFT) with the concept of pulse diversity. First, we model coherent noise jamming signal using contemporary DRFM-based chopping jamming techniques. Chopping and interleaving (C&I), and smeared spectrum (SMSP) techniques are leveraged to generate jamming signals by manipulating the internal structure of the intercepted radar signal. The deceptive jamming signal is analyzed in time and frequency domains based on the properties of the intercepted radar target. Then, we present a comprehensive analytical model for the proposed deceptive jamming suppression approach, based on phase coded waveforms to achieve pulse diversity technique. In temporal pulse diversity, we transmit the specific pulse transmission block, which cancels out the jammer spikes at an acceptable performance loss. Finally, we demonstrate the validity and capacity of the proposed methodology based on numerical results and analysis.

articleTitle: Hybrid IC based TR Module for X-band AESA Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper presented the design and development of transmit/receive (TR) module for X-band active electronically scanned array (AESA) radar. A Hybrid Microwave Integrated Circuit Technology approach using commercial off the shelf (COTS) components with sufficient high power and gain is adopted in this work. Amplitude and phase control is achieved through a GaAs core chip whereas the amplifiers are added to achieve the required gain. A medium power amplifier in the transmit path provides 1W power with more than 28 dB gain, whereas in the receive path, a LNA provides 28 dB gain with 10W receiver protection being achieved through a limiter. The transmit and receive paths are combined through a high power circulator. The TR module has been implemented on a Rogers RO4003 substrate and occupies 30 x 49 mm<sup>2</sup>.

articleTitle: Determination of Heat Fluxes for Fairing Separation of Launch Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The payload fairing is one of the most important parts of the satellite launch vehicle. It protects the satellite from severe undesired effects. Payload faring is jettisoned when it is no more required. The aerodynamic thermal flux upon fairing jettison is not greater than 1,135 W/m<sup>2</sup>. The value of heat flux can be calculated from different schemes like Direct Simulation Monte Carlo(DSMC), CFD and Navier Stokes Equation. In this paper the heat flux for fairing separation phenomenon is estimated using DSMC technique. A comparison of this estimated value with different techniques is being provided. The effects of analytical and computational heat flux schemes on payload fairing separation phenomena and payload capability of launch vehicle are also analyzed and discussed.

articleTitle: Modal Parameters Sensitivity of A Wing with Tip Mass Variation
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Due to the flexibility and light weight requirements, modern day aircraft is subjected to aeroelastic loads and instabilities. Therefore, in the aircraft design process, static and dynamic aeroelasticity has major contribution. The proposed work is focused on the numerical investigation of variation of modal parameters with variation in store mass at tip of the wing. A wing is designed in CAD software (CATIA) and analyzed for its initial structural layout in MSC Nastran. Tip mass is varied through addition of lumped masses at L.E and T.E of the structure with addition of a rod. Modal parameters sensitivity is studied for a number of combinations which would lead to a feasible cg value of a store with controlled modal parameters.

articleTitle: Shelf Life Enhancement of Polybutadiene
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Polybutadienes are prone to oxidation due to unsaturation in its structure. In order to prevent oxidation, antioxidants are usually added to Polybutadiene. Antioxidants break the degradation chain by donating H-atoms to free-radicals, thus preventing those radicals from propagating the chain reaction. The antioxidants are usually hindered phenol and aromatic amines. The most common hindered phenols are 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenol (BHT) and 2,2’-methylene-bis-(4-methyl-6-tert-butylphenol (AO 2246) or also called (CALCO 2246). Hydroxyl terminated polybutadiene was prepared by free radical polymerization of 1,3-butadiene using H<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf> as initiator. It was characterized for number average molecular weight, hydroxyl value, residual peroxide, moisture contents, polydispersity and microstructure. Two different antioxidants BHT and AO 2246 were separately added to this HTPB for stabilization against oxidation. The antioxidant activity of these two antioxidants was compared in polybutadiene hydroxyl terminated by measuring their oxidation induction temperature using DSC. The results indicate that oxidation induction temperatures obtained with AO2246 are higher as compared to those obtained with BHT which indicates a higher antioxidant activity of AO 2246. The results show that 0.1% AO 2246 is providing stabilization equal to 0.5% BHT. Accelerated aging indicate that AO2246 is providing more high temperature stabilization to polybutadiene hydroxyl terminated as compared to BHT. BHT being more volatile in nature exhibited faster depletion rate as compared to AO2246. AO2246 is a large molecule with less mobility, high melting point and boiling point, therefore, it stays more in the matrix, provides long term protection against oxidation and increases shelf life of polybutadiene hydroxyl terminated.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Bearing Only Tracking (BOT) System using Efficient Observer Trajectories
publicationTitle: 2022 19th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The main advantage of using passive target tracking is to identify the target state without exposing the presence of observing platform. The Bearing Only Tracking (BOT) is the field of underwater signal processing which is mainly focused on estimating the unknown position of target source by using the direction or angle only information. Therefore, observer can acquire the azimuth or angle information only; and cannot obtain the distance and velocity information about the target.
